TASK CONTEXT (shared):
We are porting this C++ program to pure Rust (2021 edition, std only, ZERO external crates):

    #include <iostream>
    #include <string>
    #include "../include/tsl/hopscotch_map.h"
    int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
        int count = 14;
        if (argc > 1 && std::string(argv[1]) == "--a") { count = std::stoi(argv[2]); }
        tsl::hopscotch_map<int,int> map1;
        tsl::hopscotch_map<int,int> map2;
        for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) { map1.insert({i, i*11}); map2.insert({i, i*11}); }
        std::cout << (map1 == map2) << " ";
        map2[0] = 999;
        std::cout << (map1 == map2) << std::endl;
        return 0;
    }

The tsl::hopscotch_map C++ library source is NOT available on disk and MUST NOT be read (black-box rule).
Reference binary: /workspace/dataset/test14_executable  (prints exactly the 4 bytes "1 0\n" for every valid input).
Already-verified reference-binary behavior:
  --a 0|1|3|5|10|14|100  -> "1 0\n" exit 0
  no args / "--b 5" / "x --a 5" -> "1 0\n" exit 0 (count stays 14)
  --a  (missing argv[2]) -> SIGABRT rc=134, stderr: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::logic_error'  what():  basic_string::_S_construct null not valid
  --a abc  and  --a ""   -> SIGABRT rc=134, stderr: std::invalid_argument / what(): stoi
  --a 99999999999999999999 -> SIGABRT rc=134, stderr: std::out_of_range / what(): stoi
  --a " 12" -> ok (leading ws skipped);  --a 12abc -> parses 12;  --a -5 -> ok (loop body never runs);  --a +7 -> ok;  --a 0x10 -> parses 0
  --a 2147483647 -> hangs (2 billion inserts). DO NOT run large counts; always wrap probes in `timeout 5`.
Deliverable will be a Cargo project in /output with library modules plus entry file /output/test14.rs that must ALSO
compile standalone via `rustc test14.rs` (so modules are pulled in with #[path = "..."] mod declarations, no [lib] crate).
The Rust hopscotch map must be a GENUINE hopscotch-hashing implementation written from scratch on std only
(neighborhood bitmap, displacement/swap on insert, overflow list fallback, power-of-two buckets, growth/rehash),
not a thin wrapper around std::collections::HashMap.

=== DESIGN 0 (MINIMAL-SURFACE-BUT-AUTHENTIC: five files total, exactly two library modules, zero unsafe, zero external crates. The split follows the only two real concerns in the program: (1) reproducing libstdc++/C++-runtime behavior at the process boundary (argv bytes, std::stoi, uncaught-exception terminate + SIGABRT) and (2) a genuine hopscotch hash table. Everything else — the 12 lines that mirror the C++ main() — stays in /output/test14.rs so an auditor can diff it against the original source side by side. No third "program"/"util"/"hash" module: the identity hasher is a 6-line trait living next to the table that uses it, and all impure process exits are pushed to the edge so both modules are ~100% unit-testable as pure functions (arg/stoi layer returns Result<i32, TerminateSpec>; only main() actually aborts). Dual-build is satisfied by a bin-only package (no [lib], no src/lib.rs, no src/main.rs) whose single target path is test14.rs, with modules pulled in by #[path]; verified working under `rustc test14.rs` (edition 2015 default), `rustc --edition 2021 test14.rs`, `cargo build --release`, and `cargo test` on rustc 1.75.0. DECISIONS:
- Bin-only package: [[bin]] name="test14" path="test14.rs", no [lib]/src/lib.rs/src/main.rs. This is the whole trick that makes `rustc test14.rs` and `cargo build --release` compile the identical file set. Verified end to end on rustc/cargo 1.75.0 in /tmp/layoutprobe.
- Exactly two modules (src/cxx_shim.rs, src/hopscotch_map.rs) and zero inter-module dependencies, both pulled in only from test14.rs by #[path]. No `use` of local modules at the crate root and no `crate::` paths anywhere, so the same source resolves identically under edition 2015 (rustc's default with a bare `rustc test14.rs`) and edition 2021 (cargo). If a use is wanted, it must be written `use self::cxx_shim::...;` — verified compiling in both editions.
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on line 1 of test14.rs: lint levels are lexically scoped, so it covers both #[path] modules and makes the zero-unsafe claim machine-checked rather than asserted. Empty slots use Option<(K,V)>, not MaybeUninit, which is what makes that affordable.
- Dead-code strategy is `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` on the hopscotch_map mod declaration only — NOT a blanket #![allow(dead_code)] and nothing on cxx_shim. Consequence (deliberate): under `cargo test` / `rustc --test` the lint is live, so any public map method with no unit test fails the -D warnings build. Confirmed by probe that pub-but-test-only methods do warn in a bin crate and that cfg_attr on the mod silences them for the plain build.
- Impurity is pushed to the crate edge: cxx_shim::resolve_count and cxx_stoi return Result<i32, TerminateSpec> and never touch the process; only main() calls cxx_terminate(&spec) -> writes the two lines -> flush -> std::process::abort(). This makes the entire RULE A-I recon matrix (whitespace set, sign, base-10 stop, inclusive i32 bounds, saturation, invalid-before-range ordering, argv dispatch) testable as pure assertions with no subprocess, and keeps the byte-exact strings in one const table.
- TerminateSpec as a 2-field const struct rather than free (ty, what) string pairs: the three payloads are declared once as consts (LOGIC_ERROR_NULL_STRING with `_S_construct`, INVALID_ARGUMENT_STOI, OUT_OF_RANGE_STOI) and terminate_text() is a pure formatter, so a unit test can assert the 119/87/83 byte lengths and the two-space patterns directly.
- Deterministic hashing via a tiny local `trait HopHash { fn hop_hash(&self) -> usize }` with `*self as usize` integer impls, instead of std::hash::{Hash, Hasher, BuildHasher}. Rationale: reproduces libstdc++'s identity std::hash<int> exactly (sign-extension verified: -5i32 as usize == 0xfffffffffffffffb, i32::MIN == 0xffffffff80000000), no RandomState seeding so bucket layout/displacement/overflow state is byte-reproducible run to run, ~30 fewer lines of boilerplate, and — the real payoff — tests can implement HopHash on newtype keys (Clumped -> &!0x7, Constant -> 0) to force collisions, displacement chains and the overflow list on demand.
- Bucket layout: single Vec<Bucket> of bucket_count + H - 1 entries with the u64 neighborhood bitmap and has_overflow flag stored on the home bucket next to its own Option<(K,V)> slot. Tail padding (never a home bucket) removes all modular arithmetic, so the `e - h` distance and the backward-shift window are plain subtraction. H = 62 keeps every `1u64 << j` shift inside u64 with j < 62.
- Growth/overflow policy chosen so displacement failure provably terminates: on failure, grow only while load_factor() >= MIN_LOAD_FACTOR_FOR_REHASH (0.1), otherwise push to the overflow Vec and set the home bucket's has_overflow flag. Doubling halves the load factor each attempt, so a pathological constant hasher grows a bounded number of times (62 same-home keys settle at 1024 buckets) and then uses overflow instead of looping forever.
- PartialEq is hand-written (size, then per-element other.get(k) and value compare) and Eq is gated on V: Eq; #[derive(PartialEq)] is explicitly forbidden by comment because it would compare slot order, bitmaps, bucket_count and the overflow Vec. IndexMut is implemented as insert-then-re-resolve-the-slot (hopscotch relocates on insert, so no slot index may be cached across it) and inserts V::default() when absent — this is the single semantic that makes `--a 0` / `--a -5` print `1 0` instead of `1 1`.
- insert(k, v) -> bool with tsl/std no-overwrite semantics; overwrite lives in a separate insert_or_assign(k, v) -> Option<V>. Unit-tested explicitly even though the program never inserts a duplicate.
- Unit tests live inline as #[cfg(test)] mod tests inside each module file (the only option without a lib target — tests/ cannot import a bin) and the single tests/cli.rs drives the built binary through CARGO_BIN_EXE_test14, restating the expected byte strings independently of the module consts. Bonus: `rustc --test test14.rs` runs the unit tests with no cargo at all — verified.
- Five files total, no README/report/doc files, no build.rs, no dev-dependencies, no feature flags. Module-level //! docs carry the audit narrative (invariants I1-I3, the tsl semantics being mirrored) instead of a separate document.
RISKS:
- Edition drift between the two required build commands: `rustc test14.rs` compiles as edition 2015, cargo as 2021. Everything must be edition-neutral — no array `.into_iter()` by value (2015/2018 yields references), no reliance on TryFrom/TryInto being in the prelude, no `panic!(non_literal_expr)`, no `dyn`-less trait objects, and no let-chains (not in 1.75 anyway). Add a CI-style one-liner to the acceptance check: `rustc -D warnings test14.rs && rustc --edition 2021 -D warnings test14.rs && cargo build --release && cargo test`.
- The `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` on the map module means the plain build cannot catch genuinely-orphaned code; if the public surface listed here grows without a matching unit test, `cargo test -- -D warnings` (or a #![deny] in test cfg) is the only thing that will notice. Keep the surface at the listed size or trim it — every extra method is another test obligation.
- cxx_shim has NO dead-code allowance, so any const or helper that ends up unused (e.g. a TerminateSpec const only referenced from tests/cli.rs, which cannot import it) will fail `rustc -D warnings`. Make sure all three consts are reachable from resolve_count/cxx_stoi in the non-test build.
- The #[cfg(not(unix))] argv fallback is never compiled on the grading host, so it is unverified and unlinted. Keep it to two lines (to_string_lossy -> into_owned -> into_bytes) or drop it entirely and accept a unix-only build; a broken cfg branch is worse than an absent one.
- Overflow-list activation depends on the interaction of H, max_load_factor and MIN_LOAD_FACTOR_FOR_REHASH. With H=62 and mlf 0.95 the Constant-hasher test grows to ~1024 buckets before overflowing; if those constants are tuned, that test can either become slow (many rehashes) or stop exercising overflow at all. Assert overflow_len() > 0 explicitly rather than inferring it, and cap the test at ~64 keys.
- Shift and index hazards in the displacement chain: `1u64 << j` must only be evaluated for j < H (H=62 keeps this safe, but a later bump to 64 makes it a debug panic), and the backward-shift window `e-(H-1) ..= e-1` underflows on usize when e < H-1 — that branch is unreachable only because `e - h >= H` implies e >= H, which must be stated as a debug_assert or the code will panic in debug on a subtle refactor.
- The classic hopscotch bug the reviewer will look for: updating the bitmap of the slot written to instead of the HOME bucket, or forgetting the clear-bit half of a move. assert_invariants() must re-derive each set bit's home from the stored key (not from bookkeeping) and compare popcount-sum + overflow_len against len, and it must be called after every mutation in every table test — otherwise the whole layout's authenticity claim rests on unverified code, since the reference binary's output is `1 0` for all counts and proves nothing about the machinery.
- tests/cli.rs asserting SIGABRT: status.code() is None for signal-killed children, so it must use ExitStatusExt::signal() == Some(6) under #[cfg(unix)]; asserting 134 via code() will fail even when the port is byte-correct. Also invoke the binary directly (never through `timeout`/a shell) or the wrapper's `dumped core` line and bash's `Aborted` job message pollute the stderr comparison.
- The differential test must be skipped when /workspace/dataset/test14_executable is missing, and must never pass a large count — `--a 2147483647` hangs for billions of inserts in both the reference and the port. Cap the test matrix at 5000 and keep any exploratory probe under `timeout 5`.
- Cargo target autodiscovery: adding anything under /output/src/bin/ or creating src/main.rs or src/lib.rs later would introduce a competing target and break the single-entry-file guarantee (autobins=false in the manifest guards the src/bin case only). The two modules must stay as plain non-target files under src/.
- Float load-factor arithmetic (f32 max_load_factor) recomputed per insert is both a hot-path cost and a source of off-by-one growth thresholds across bucket sizes; derive a usize load_threshold once per grow/rehash and compare integers, or the growth boundary tests become platform-rounding sensitive.
- stdout flushing: relying on println!'s LineWriter plus runtime flush-at-exit is correct today, but any future early `std::process::exit` or abort added after a print would drop the 4 bytes. Keep abort strictly confined to the pre-print argument phase, as the layout does.

- No [lib] target at all: one [[bin]] name="test14" path="test14.rs", every module reached via #[path = "src/..."] mod from the entry file. Verified on rustc/cargo 1.75.0 that this satisfies BOTH `rustc -D warnings -O test14.rs` and `cargo build --release`/`cargo test` (unit tests inside the bin crate ran). Nested modules work because a #[path]-included mod.rs resolves its children relative to its own directory, so src/hopscotch/mod.rs finds src/hopscotch/bucket.rs with a plain `pub mod bucket;` — no per-file #[path] needed below the top level.
- Per-module inner `#![allow(dead_code)]` (in src/cxx/mod.rs, src/hash/mod.rs, src/hopscotch/mod.rs, src/app/mod.rs) rather than a crate-root allow or Cargo's [lints] table. Measured: under -D warnings an unused `pub fn` in a bin crate is a hard error (`error: function 'unused_api' is never used ... -D dead-code implied by -D warnings`), and tsl-parity API is ~90% unused by main, so this is mandatory. Cargo [lints] is rejected as unportable since `rustc test14.rs` never reads Cargo.toml. Module-scoped allows also keep the entry file clean and document why (library surface, not bin surface).
- Errors as values, aborts only at the boundary: cxx::stoi::stoi and app::count::resolve_count return Result<i32, CxxThrow>, and only main_impl calls cxx::terminate. This is a deliberate departure from the recon's reference snippet (which calls cxx_terminate inside cxx_stoi and is therefore untestable in-process), and it structurally guarantees the 'stdout empty on every abort path' rule because no writer is constructed until resolve_count returns Ok.
- Exception text lives in one data type (CxxThrow with exception_type()/what()/message_bytes()) so the 119/87/83-byte payloads are asserted by unit tests in two places. I measured the reference binary's `--a` stderr at exactly 119 bytes, which resolves the internal contradiction in the recon: RECON 2's parenthetical 'program's own stderr is 118 bytes' is an off-by-one; RECON 1's 119 is correct.
- std::hash::{Hash, Hasher, BuildHasher} for real generic parity, with `HopscotchMap<K, V, S = BuildIdentityHasher>` plus a separate concrete-S impl block providing new()/with_capacity() so callers never need a turbofish and inference never fails. IdentityHasher makes write_i32/write_u64 the identity (reproducing libstdc++ std::hash<int>, sign-extension included) and folds byte-writing keys with FNV-1a so String keys are testable. No RandomState anywhere in the crate.
- Adversarial hashers (BuildConstantHasher, BuildMaskHasher, BuildStrideHasher) ship as real library items in src/hash/collide.rs, not test-local helpers. test14's key pattern produces zero collisions, zero displacements and an always-empty overflow list, so these are the only way the hopscotch machinery gets exercised at all — they deserve documented, warning-clean code.
- Three-way split of the container: bucket.rs owns all bit manipulation (confining the canonical 'updated the wrong bucket's bitmap' bug to one small file), table.rs owns the algorithm and storage with zero API sugar, map.rs owns the tsl-shaped surface and trait impls, and invariants.rs adds a second impl block on HopscotchTable so the verifier can grow without inflating the core.
- PartialEq is hand-written (size check, then per-element get on the other map) and #[derive(PartialEq)] is explicitly banned — deriving would compare slot order, bitmaps and bucket_count, breaking the order-independence tsl's free operator== guarantees. Eq only where V: Eq.
- IndexMut<&K> is implemented (K: Clone, V: Default) as insert-then-return-&mut, mirroring C++ operator[]'s default-insert; Index<&Q> (Borrow-generic) is the panicking `at`. IndexMut's supertrait Index<&K> is satisfied by the Borrow-generic impl with Q = K, so no extra impl and no coherence conflict. This is what makes `map2[&0] = 999` both compile and yield `1 0` for count <= 0.
- Storage is Vec<Bucket> + Vec<Slot<K,V>> with slots.len() == bucket_count + NEIGHBORHOOD_SIZE - 1 (padding, never modular wraparound, exactly like tsl), and Slot is an enum with take()/fill(). Displacement moves elements by value through Slot::take, so the whole algorithm is expressible under #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at the crate root — zero-unsafe is compiler-enforced, not merely claimed.
- H = 62 in a u64 bitmap with `const _: () = assert!(NEIGHBORHOOD_SIZE <= 63);` and every shift routed through Bucket methods that debug_assert j < H, closing the `1u64 << 64` overflow-panic / UB-shift trap.
- Invariant verification is an always-compiled method invoked explicitly from tests, never a #[cfg(debug_assertions)]-gated fn called from debug_assert!. Rationale: debug_assert! bodies are still type-checked and compiled in release, so a cfg-gated helper would break `cargo build --release`; and an O(n) verify per insert would make the churn tests quadratic. Checkpoint verification in tests gets equal coverage at usable speed.
- Two test tiers: (a) src/tests/* pulled in under #[cfg(test)] from test14.rs, giving crate-internal access to table internals with no lib target (verified excluded from plain `rustc test14.rs`, included by both `cargo test` and `rustc --test test14.rs`); (b) tests/cli.rs using env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_test14") to spawn the real binary and assert rc/signal(6)/stdout/stderr bytes against the reference executable — verified working with no [lib], and skipping gracefully when the reference is absent so `cargo test` stays portable.
- The insert loop uses i.wrapping_mul(11) so a hypothetical huge count cannot turn C++ UB into a Rust debug overflow panic (which would print panic text and exit 101 instead of matching), and stdout is written once, after validation, from the derived bools via `as u8` — never Display on a bool, never a hardcoded "1 0".
RISKS:
- Warning budget is the most likely build-breaker: under -D warnings a rich API in a bin crate trips dead_code (measured as a hard error), and #[cfg(test)]-only helpers also trip unused_* in non-test builds. The per-module #![allow(dead_code)] handles that, but anything else (unused_variables, unused_mut in the displacement loop, unused_imports in src/tests/*) must be fixed rather than allowed. Gate CI on both `rustc -D warnings test14.rs` and `RUSTFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo test`, since the two crates differ in what is reachable.
- Infinite-loop/OOM hazard in the grow/probe/displace retry path. With BuildConstantHasher every key homes to bucket 0, so growth never reduces clustering and a 'displacement failed -> grow -> retry' loop that does not fall through to the overflow list will spin or allocate forever. The overflow list must be an unconditional escape hatch and the retry must be a bounded loop (at most one grow per insert attempt), not recursion. The 10k-constant-hash-keys test exists to catch this and should be written before the growth code.
- ExactSizeIterator honesty: chaining slot iteration with overflow iteration through filter_map cannot report an exact len, so an explicit `remaining` counter must be threaded through every iterator. Getting this wrong makes collect()/size_hint subtly wrong and violates the ExactSizeIterator contract while still passing naive tests.
- IndexMut's bound set (K: Clone, V: Default) is narrower than Index's and will surprise callers with non-Clone keys; it also means the call site reads `map2[&0] = 999` rather than the C++ `map2[0] = 999`. Acceptable and documented, but state it in map.rs docs so it is not later 'fixed' by adding a by-value Index impl that would collide with the Borrow-generic one.
- Generic-parameter creep: making growth policy a fourth type parameter would force turbofish at nearly every construction site and break inference on HopscotchMap::new(). Keeping PowerOfTwoGrowth as a concrete field behind a trait gives library shape without the ergonomics tax, at the cost of a small refactor if an alternative policy is ever needed.
- Determinism cuts both ways: identity hashing reproduces the reference layout exactly but is pathological for keys that are multiples of the bucket count. Churn tests must include those strides, otherwise the port looks healthy on 0..n keys (all test14 exercises) while degrading badly on realistic input.
- tests/cli.rs hazards: never pass a large count (--a 2147483647 hangs for minutes / OOMs — cap probes at 65536), do not assume status.code() is Some on abort paths (it is None; use ExitStatusExt::signal() == Some(6)), and do not compare stderr captured through a `timeout` wrapper (it injects 'timeout: the monitored command dumped core'). Spawning the binary directly, as designed, avoids the wrapper noise entirely.
- File count is high (~30). If time runs short the safe collapse order is: fold src/hash/collide.rs into src/hash/mod.rs, fold growth.rs and config.rs into table.rs, and merge the eight src/tests/* files into three. Do NOT collapse table.rs/map.rs (loses algorithm-vs-API separation), bucket.rs (loses the bit-manipulation containment that prevents the canonical hopscotch bug), or cxx/* (loses testability of the abort payloads).
- The recon's 118-vs-119 discrepancy means at least one measurement was wrong; the design pins the value in throw.rs behind a unit-tested length constant and cross-checks it against the live reference in tests/cli.rs. If the grading machine's reference binary differs (e.g. a libstdc++ emitting _M_construct), that single constant is the only place needing a change — re-measure against the actual grading binary before finalizing.
- `cargo test` compiles the bin as a test harness, so main() never runs and the abort behavior is untested in-process; tests/cli.rs is the only thing exercising cxx::terminate for real. If it is dropped for portability the abort paths lose all coverage — keep it with skip-if-absent rather than deleting it.

They are unobservable through this program, so no test can pin them; the risk is not wrongness but a reviewer reading them as verified facts. input.rationale:
DESIGN 1 wins (37/40) on the maintainability-and-testability lens, with two mechanical defects that Design 2 has already diagnosed with receipts.

Decisive factor: I compiled the 1,688 lines already sitting in /output/src/tsl/ and they ARE Design 1's architecture — std Hash/Hasher/BuildHasher with identity integer paths plus an FNV-1a byte fold, a Position enum for slot-vs-overflow, Borrow-generic Q lookups, iterators with explicit `remaining` counters implementing ExactSizeIterator and FusedIterator, tail-padded slot array, `hop_empty_closer` backward displacement selecting the closest movable element, push_overflow, integer load_threshold, rehash-through-the-normal-path, assert_invariants. Design 1 is the only design whose spec is nearly a description of working code; Design 0 would discard all of it (custom HopHash trait, single-file map, no Borrow generics, no iterator suite) and Design 2 would rename it (HashPolicy<K> vs the on-disk CppStdHash, set_neighbor vs set_present, hopscotch_hash.rs vs table.rs) despite claiming reconciliation.

Algorithmic authenticity is where Design 1 separates hardest (10 vs 9/7). Confining every bit operation to bucket.rs is the strongest structural defense against the canonical hopscotch bug (updating the written-to slot's bitmap instead of the HOME bucket's). Its Vec+free-list OverflowList with opaque handles looked like over-engineering until I checked the on-disk code: table.rs returns Position::Overflow(index) from find and insert but removes with Vec::remove(index), which shifts and silently invalidates every later overflow position — Design 1's handle design prevents exactly that by construction. It also uniquely notes that debug_assert! bodies are type-checked in release, so the invariant verifier must be always-compiled rather than cfg(debug_assertions)-gated, and it correctly keeps growth policy as a concrete field behind a trait to avoid a fourth generic parameter breaking inference on new(). I separately verified its trickiest coherence claim: a Borrow-generic Index<&Q> does satisfy the IndexMut<&K> supertrait at Q=K, and `m[&0] = 999` default-inserts on an empty map in both editions — the load-bearing line for `--a 0` printing `1 0`.

Its two real defects are cheap to fix and both come from Design 2's empirical work. First, bare `rustc test14.rs` compiles at edition 2015, where `pub use table::HopscotchTable;` fails E0432 — I reproduced this on the actual on-disk modules; Design 1 writes that broken form in all four of its mod.rs facades while claiming the scheme was mechanically verified. Second, and sharper, `#![allow(dead_code)]` does NOT cover unused_imports: with the module-level allow in place, the facade re-export still hard-errored under -D warnings. Design 1's entire warning strategy is per-module allow(dead_code), so its facades are unprotected. Both are one-line-per-site fixes, not architectural, which is why they cost fidelity/idiomatic points rather than the win.

Design 2 (34) is the best-researched design and the most disciplined about the process boundary — golden.rs as a single source of truth with 119/87/83 length tripwires (I re-measured all three against the reference and confirmed them), the _S_construct-not-_M_construct trap, absent-vs-empty argv[2], c_isspace vs is_ascii_whitespace, signal() vs code(), and by far the best integration artifact: a true differential that compares rc+signal+stdout+stderr against the reference with its own spawn/try_wait/kill timeout, since std's Command::output() has none. But it loses on two counts. Its custom HashPolicy<K> trait is less idiomatic than std BuildHasher AND conflicts with the code already on disk, and its KeyEqual<K> is left undecided ("or just rely on K: Eq"). More seriously, golden.rs defines STDOUT_SUCCESS = b"1 0\n" and instructs main to "emit exactly b'1 0\n'" — a fidelity trap that invites hardcoding the answer, which would pass every differential probe while the map does nothing. That is the one thing a port must never do, and Design 1 is the only design that explicitly bans it.

Design 0 (30) is the weakest for this brief despite the single best testability mechanism in the set: `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]`, which I verified keeps plain builds clean while hard-erroring on any untested public method under --test. But the design itself collapses the map, iterators, invariants, overflow, and growth into one ~650-line file, drops Borrow-generic lookups (get(&self, k: &K) only), returns `impl Iterator` and so forfeits ExactSizeIterator honesty, and has the weakest integration layer (largely hardcoded assertions, differential optional, no timeout, no oracle-based churn). Its minimalism buys auditability of the 12-line main — worth grafting as a principle — but under-delivers the "library-grade, genuinely testable container" the task asks for.

Net: build on Design 1, apply Design 2's edition/lint/timeout/differential findings and Design 0's coverage tripwire, and reconcile onto the existing src/tsl/ names rather than renaming working code.
